name: Marfan Syndrome

criteria.description: Aortic root dilation (Z-score >= 2) or aortic dissection
FBN1 mutation known to be associated with Marfan syndrome
Systemic score >= 7 points (using revised Ghent scoring system)
Pectus excavatum or chest asymmetry (1 point)
Reduced upper segment/lower segment ratio AND increased arm span/height (1 point)
Facial features (dolichocephaly, enophthalmos, downslanting palpebral fissures, malar hypoplasia, retrognathia) (1 point)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Without family history: (1) Aortic root dilation (Z >= 2) + ectopia lentis = MFS; (2) Aortic root dilation + FBN1 = MFS; (3) Aortic root dilation + systemic score >= 7 = MFS; (4) Ectopia lentis + FBN1 known to cause aortic disease = MFS. With family history: (1) Ectopia lentis + family history = MFS; (2) Systemic score >= 7 + family history = MFS; (3) Aortic root dilation (Z >= 2 for adults, Z >= 3 for <20) + family history = MFS.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: The revised Ghent nosology emphasizes aortic root dilation/dissection and ectopia lentis as cardinal features.

pathognomonic.notes: Progressive; Z-score >= 2 at the sinuses of Valsalva

common.symptomName: Disproportionately tall stature with long limbs
common.notes: Reduced upper-to-lower segment ratio; increased arm span-to-height ratio
searchTerms: very tall with long arms and legs
disproportionate tall height with long limbs
excessive limb length causing tall stature

occasional.notes: Lumbosacral dural ectasia; may cause low back pain

laboratory: TGF-beta levels may be elevated (research setting)
imaging: Echocardiography: aortic root measurement at sinuses of Valsalva with Z-score calculation
CT/MR angiography for comprehensive aortic assessment
MRI lumbosacral spine for dural ectasia
Skeletal radiographs for protrusio acetabuli assessment
genetic: FBN1 (fibrillin-1) mutations: identified in >95% of cases meeting revised Ghent criteria
TGFBR1/TGFBR2 testing to exclude Loeys-Dietz syndrome

distinguishingFeatures: LDS has widespread arterial tortuosity and aneurysms
LDS may feature bifid uvula/cleft palate and hypertelorism
vEDS lacks tall stature and ectopia lentis
hEDS lacks aortic root dilation and ectopia lentis
hEDS does not feature marfanoid habitus
Stickler has vitreoretinal degeneration and retinal detachment
Stickler features midface hypoplasia and hearing loss
Stickler caused by COL2A1, COL11A1, COL11A2

redFlags: Acute severe chest or back pain (suspect aortic dissection - emergency)
Sudden vision loss (retinal detachment or lens dislocation)
Aortic root diameter approaching 5 cm (surgical threshold)
Family history of aortic dissection or sudden cardiac death
references: Loeys BL, et al. The revised Ghent nosology for the Marfan syndrome. J Med Genet. 2010;47(7):476-85.
Dietz HC. Marfan Syndrome. In: GeneReviews. University of Washington, Seattle; Updated 2022.
Judge DP, Dietz HC. Marfan's syndrome. Lancet. 2005;366(9501):1965-76.
Lacro RV, et al. Atenolol versus losartan in children and young adults with Marfan's syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2014;371(22):2061-71.
commonPitfalls: Often misdiagnosed as other connective tissue disorders due to overlapping features such as joint hypermobility and skin findings.
Aortic root dilation may be missed if echocardiography is not performed or interpreted correctly.
Ectopia lentis can be subtle and overlooked without a thorough ophthalmologic exam.
Tall stature and long limbs may be attributed to normal familial tallness or constitutional growth patterns.

extendedDiscriminators.feature: Marfan syndrome typically lacks the bifid uvula, hypertelorism, and arterial tortuosity seen in Loeys-Dietz syndrome.
Marfan syndrome features aortic root dilation and ectopia lentis, which are not characteristic of vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
Marfan syndrome presents with aortic root dilation and lens dislocation, which are absent in hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
Marfan syndrome is distinguished by ectopia lentis and aortic root dilation, while Stickler syndrome more commonly presents with midface hypoplasia, cleft palate, and vitreoretinal degeneration.

ruleOutCriteria: Absence of aortic root dilation on serial echocardiography in an adult with otherwise suggestive features.
Normal lens position (no ectopia lentis) on comprehensive ophthalmologic examination.
Negative genetic testing for pathogenic FBN1 mutations in a patient meeting revised Ghent criteria.
